summary: Redwood AE/SE ran an Optimize-focused walkthrough for NexaHealth exploring quantization profiles (INT8 and FP8), tradeoffs between latency and quality, and a proposed benchmarking plan. Customer is evaluating Dedicated vs Hosted for production; main concerns: latency SLOs for interactive triage, quality degradation with aggressive quant, and audit/security requirements.
topics: Quality vs latency comparisons and evaluation metrics
Demo: applying profiles and viewing predicted token-level latency impact
Benchmarking plan and next steps (sample set, infra)
transcript:
Header: 2025-08-19 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~58m | Attendees: Alexei Morozov (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), James Park (CTO, NexaHealth), Maya Singh (ML Engineer), Lena Rodriguez (Infra Lead)

[00:00] Alexei: hey everyone, thanks for joining, can you all hear me ok?
[00:04] James: yes, loud and clear. thanks Alexei.
[00:07] Priya: hi! Priya here from the SE side, i'll be driving the Optimize demo today, alexei will cover pricing / next steps.
[00:14] James: awesome. quick FYI, we have a hard latency SLO of 250ms p95 for our triage assistant, and cost is pretty important but we care more about quality.
[00:26] Alexei: got it, that's helpful context. Maya, Lena, anything to add?
[00:30] Maya: we use a variant of the llama family rn, 13B-ish, and we see token runtime around 60ms/token on our infra. we're curious whether INT8 or FP8 gets us under the SLO without losing clinical QA.
[00:45] Lena: and from infra, we need to understand memory reductions and whether VPC/on-prem deploy is feasible later, also KMS integration for keys.

[01:02] Priya: ok jumping into the console, i'm in Optimize -> Quantization profiles. you'll see we have prebuilt profiles for INT8 and FP8, also hybrid profiles labeled "int8+kv-cache" etc. note: some names might appear slightly different in the transcript, recorded autotext can mis-spell.
[01:29] Priya: (shares screen) here is the quality delta view - we plot task-specific metric (ROUGE/QA-F1) vs latency change relative to fp16 baseline. FP8 typically shows ~1-2% quality delta, INT8 sometimes 3-6% depending on layer folding and per-channel quantization.
[01:48] James: can you make that concrete - for our 13B model what's expected p95 improvement?
[01:53] Priya: yes, so for a 13B baseline on A100-like, FP8 often gives ~1.7x token throughput, INT8 nearer 2.5x but with higher repro/quality variance. p95 latency improvement depends on batching and KV-cache usage; with small live batch sizes FP8 may actually win because fewer dequant ops.
[02:20] Maya: when you say quality delta, is that on our clinical prompt set or general benchmarks?
[02:25] Priya: this view is generalized, but you can upload custom prompt sets - we recommend running a short eval on your 500-2k prompts to get a projected delta. that is part of the benchmark plan.

[03:00] Alexei: quick note on safety/audit: all quantized runs keep policy logs and we can map outputs back to input tokens which helps QA. SOC2 docs are in the security pack we'll send.
[03:18] James: great. one concern: does INT8 change hallucination patterns?
[03:23] Priya: good question. generally INT8 can amplify some distributional errors, particularly on rarely seen tokens; we flag those in Optimize's regression alerts. FP8 tends to be safer. we also support mixed precision per-layer to reduce regression.

[04:05] Priya: demo step: create a profile. selecting model family -> 13B-llama-variant (approx). choose target quant: int8, fp8, or hybrid. i'll select FP8 first.
[04:27] Priya: here's the "predicted latency impact" slider - it's an estimate from our runtime profiler. for FP8 it predicts ~45% token latency reduction for your average sequence length of 64, INT8 predicts ~65%. remember that's a distribution and depends on KV-cache hits.
[04:50] James: ok that's promising. how do you measure the quality delta? is it automatic?
[04:55] Priya: Optimize runs a head-to-head evaluation using your prompt set if available or our default benchmarks, computes task metrics (F1, bleu, etc) and also does a small human-in-the-loop sample check if requested. results surface as numeric delta and example-level diffs.

[05:35] Maya: can we see an example diff?
[05:38] Priya: yep pulling one up - here's baseline fp16 output vs fp8 vs int8 for a sample triage prompt. fp8 preserves the medical term, int8 clipped an uncertain token and replaced it with a more generic phrase - you can see the token-level probabilities are lower for the rare token under INT8.
[05:58] James: that aligns with our concerns - losing specifics could break downstream triage rules.

[06:20] Priya: that's why Optimize suggests "guardrails" - you can apply a higher-precision pass for specific token ranges or layers (per-layer fallback) and that hybrid approach gets you most of the latency gains while protecting critical token generation.
[06:40] Alexei: and from product standpoint, customers often do FP8 for first pass and layer-fallback for medical terms. Cost delta vs fp16 typically ~35-60% savings depending on profile.

[07:12] James: show us memory reduction numbers too?
[07:16] Priya: sure - FP8 reduces model memory footprint ~2x vs fp16, INT8 closer to 3x. that affects max batch size and whether you can host multiple replicas per GPU. for Dedicated this is attractive.

[07:48] Lena: on VPC/private: do these quant tools run in private deployments or only hosted?
[07:52] Priya: they run in all deployments; Optimize is available in Private and Dedicated - console may be controlled by the private control plane for on-prem. KMS integrations for key material are supported per-customer. some profiling telemetry is optional and can be disabled for air-gapped setups.

[08:20] Priya: next, quality vs latency plot - (points) here's an example of a client that needed <200ms p95; they used FP8 + KV-cache + small per-layer fallback on output layer and achieved p95 185ms with 1.4% quality delta - they accepted that. another client with stricter QA used hybrid approach and got p95 220ms with 0.5% delta.
[08:47] James: helpful. how do we operationalize regression monitoring?
[08:51] Priya: Optimize can register baseline evals and create regression alerts tied to prompt sets. when a quanted rollout hits x% degradation we trigger a canary rollback. you can tune thresholds per bucket.

[09:26] James: any gotchas for models trained with rotary embeddings or other custom ops?
[09:30] Priya: yes some kernel incompatibilities show up. our runtime compiles model graphs and picks kernels; for rare ops we recommend FP8 fallback. we do a compatibility scan during profile creation and highlight risky ops.

[10:02] Maya: can we run a quick local benchmark during this call? we have a tiny dataset ready.
[10:07] Alexei: yes let's schedule a dedicated bench; Priya can kick it off - we also often run an initial 500-prompt smoke test during onboarding.
[10:15] Priya: i'll note that as an action item.

[12:00] [screen share pause, brief side convo]
[13:10] Priya: returning to demo - here's how to apply a profile to a production route. you can attach profile to a model alias; rollout options include canary % and automatic fallback to fp16 or another variant if quality drops.
[13:35] Priya: (minor transcription glitch) the UI shows predicted cost per 1M tokens too, which is helpful - FP8 often ~40% cheaper than fp16, INT8 ~55% cheaper in many cases.

[14:00] James: curious about batch sizing - our application is low concurrency but many short sequences. does batching help?
[14:06] Priya: with low concurrency and short sequences, KV-cache reuse helps more than batching; Optimize recommends small batches and aggressive caching. INT8's larger throughput advantage shows up more under larger batch sizes.

[15:00] Lena: on infra, what GPUs did you assume for the numbers?
[15:04] Priya: A100 and H100 baselines in the profiler; for cost estimates we show g5 (NVIDIA A10G-like) and p4-like numbers too. we can re-run with your target hardware if you share it.

[16:20] James: ok, let's talk rollout plan - we want to test on a subset of traffic and run for two weeks before committing.
[16:26] Alexei: standard approach: bench on sample set, then canary 5-10% with continuous eval, and if regression < threshold we ramp. we can include a manual approval gate.

[17:05] Maya: what about model ops for hot code reloads if we use per-layer fallback?
[17:09] Priya: fallbacks are handled in the runtime - it's an execution-time decision, not a code change. you can toggle at route level.

[18:30] James: any examples of customers who moved entirely to INT8?

[18:34] Priya: a few experimental customers in recommendation use INT8 aggressively where hallucination tolerance is higher. most regulated workflows prefer FP8 or hybrid.

[20:00] Priya: switching to the recommended benchmark plan: step 1 upload prompt set and baseline outputs, step 2 run head-to-head fp16 vs fp8 vs int8, step 3 review diffs and pick per-layer fallbacks, step 4 canary rollout.

[21:15] Alexei: i'll follow up with pricing scenarios for Hosted vs Dedicated including expected savings with FP8/INT8. for Dedicated we can show reserved capacity and expected throughput per GPU with these profiles.

[22:40] Maya: any compliance issues with quantized models and auditability?
[22:44] Priya: quantization doesn't affect logging; we still have full request/response logs, token-level attribution, and the same retention controls. KMS/HSM are available.

[24:10] [brief cross talk about internal timelines]

[25:00] James: timeline - if we like results, we could start pilot in September and go into production by November.

[26:12] Priya: note on tooling: Optimize exposes an API so you can automate profile application as part of CI for model changes.

[28:00] Alexei: ok let's recap real quick - action items, priya will run bench, i'll send security/pricing, maya provide prompt set. any other items?

[28:15] James: also please include an example of per-layer fallback config.

[28:40] Priya: will do.

[29:00] [wrap up pleasantries]

[30:00] Recording note: transcript may contain some ASR artifacts.

End of call.
